drafted_from: tool:export-records-as-list-rows row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json), do-work/export_records_as_list_rows.py, read-data/list_rows.py and test/test_list_rows.py; the answer is what the script printed on the same made-up bakery input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn my bakery orders in data/orders.json into rows for my orders list with the mapping I wrote, and tell me how many rows came out."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: every list and column comes from the mapping, and it only writes payload files into a folder and sends nothing.
instructions: 1. Put your records in a folder (here data/orders.json holding {"orders":[{"id":"O-1","customer":"Sam","item":"sourdough loaf","qty":"2","status":"paid"}, ...]}) and write mapping.json: new_lists names the list and its fields, and each source names the file, the path to the records, the row id template and a map saying how each field is made (from, number, choice with a table, const).
2. Say "Turn my records into rows"; your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:export-records-as-list-rows"} and runs its command with {mapping}, {root} and {out} filled in.
3. Read the counts it prints and open manifest.json and the orders-000.json batch in the out folder; a refusal on stderr (exit 2) says what to change, for example two records making one row id.
4. Nothing has been sent yet: when you agree, put the batches into your list with tool:send-list-row-batches.

worked_examples.title: Two bakery orders become two list rows
worked_examples.ask: Turn my bakery orders in data/orders.json into rows for my orders list.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of tools/export-records-as-list-rows/do-work/export_records_as_list_rows.py on made-up input (the toy-library mapping in test/test_list_rows.py uses the same keys). The AI runs: python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/export-records-as-list-rows/do-work/export_records_as_list_rows.py --mapping mapping.json --root bakery --out payloads. data/orders.json holds O-1 (Sam, sourdough loaf, qty "2", status paid) and O-2 (Ana, rye bun, qty "12", status open); the mapping maps customer and item with from, qty with number, and status with choice and the table paid to Paid, open to Open.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"orders": {"list_id": "orders", "rows": 2}}, exit 0. payloads/ holds make_lists.json, manifest.json and orders-000.json: {"list_id": "orders", "rows": [{"id": "O-1", "values": {"customer": "Sam", "item": "sourdough loaf", "qty": 2, "status": "Paid"}}, {"id": "O-2", "values": {"customer": "Ana", "item": "rye bun", "qty": 12, "status": "Open"}}]}.
